{{nihongo|'''Amatsu Shrine'''|天津神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Echigo Province]].

'''Amatsu Shrine''' (あまつじんじゃ) is a {{jalink|神社|Q845945}} located in Ichinomiya, {{jalink|糸魚川市|Q857208}}, {{jalink|新潟県|Q132705}}. It is a {{jalink|式内社}} {{jalink|論社|Q135022904}} and claims the title of {{jalink|一宮|Q1656379}} of {{jalink|越後国|Q666514}}. Its former {{jalink|近代社格制度|Q712534|旧社格}} was {{jalink|県社}}.

== Overview ==
It is said to have been founded during the reign of {{jalink|景行天皇|Q329723}}, and is also said to have been a prayer site (chokuganjo) of {{jalink|孝徳天皇|Q317980}}. It was venerated as the {{jalink|産土神|Q1392097}} (tutelary deity) of the Ichinomiya, Oshiage, Teramachi, Ōmachi, and Shichikenmachi districts, among others, of the former {{jalink|糸魚川町|Q11604888}}. In the 16th year of {{jalink|慶長|Q1328185}} ({{jalink|1611年|Q6768}}), the {{jalink|江戸幕府|Q205662}} donated one hundred koku of kuro-indi land, which was converted to vermilion-seal land (shuinchi) the following year. In the 7th year of {{jalink|大正|Q329174}} ({{jalink|1918年|Q2094}}), it was listed as a gōsha (village shrine) and was later elevated to ken-sha (prefectural shrine).

In the ''{{jalink|延喜式神名帳|Q11064932}}'', a {{jalink|式内社}} listed as "{{jalink|越後国|Q666514}} {{jalink|頸城郡|Q11664982}} Great Shrine (Ōjinja)" is identified with this shrine as one of its {{jalink|論社|Q135022904}} (candidate shrines). Additionally, the Nunagawa Shrine within the {{jalink|境内社}} (shrine precincts) is also a shikinaisha ronsha.

== Deities ==
* Center: {{jalink|ニニギ|Q1056017|天津彦々火瓊々杵尊}} (Amatsuhikohikohononinigi no Mikoto)
* Left: {{jalink|天児屋根命}} (Amenokoyane no Mikoto)
* Right: {{jalink|太玉命}} (Futodama no Mikoto)

== Subsidiary Shrines ==
[[File:Amatsu-jinja (Itoigawa), Nunagawa-jinja.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Nunagawa Shrine}}]]
* Nunagawa Shrine
*: {{jalink|奴奈川姫命}} is enshrined as the principal deity, and {{jalink|大国主|Q276944}} (Yachimata no Mikoto) was later merged into worship. This area was formerly known as "Numakawa-gō," and there is an account in {{jalink|日本神話|Q814158}} ({{jalink|大国主の神話|Q11433656}}) in which Yachimata no Mikoto visited {{jalink|奴奈川姫命}} who lived here. According to tradition, the child born to the two deities was {{jalink|建御名方命}}, who traveled up the {{jalink|姫川|Q11447417}} river into {{jalink|信濃国|Q289250}} and developed the land there.
*: It is listed as one of the 13 shrines of {{jalink|頸城郡|Q11664982}} in the ''{{jalink|延喜式神名帳|Q11064932}}''. In addition to this shrine, there are multiple shrines named "Nunagawa Shrine" within Kubiki District, including {{jalink|奴奈川神社}} (former gōsha) in Tabuse-Minamimura, Itoigawa City, and {{jalink|能生白山神社|Q11611996|白山神社}} (former gōsha) in Ōaza Nōmiya no Kami, Itoigawa City — both of which are also considered ronsha of the shikinaisha Nunagawa Shrine.
<gallery>
File:Amatsu-jinja (Itoigawa), keidaisha.jpg|Subsidiary shrines (keidaisha)
</gallery>

== Festivals and Ceremonies ==
The shrine is known for its bugaku (court music and dance) performances ({{jalink|天津神社舞楽|Q11442800}}), commonly called the "Chigo no Mai" (Children's Dance), which are performed as offerings at the April annual festival.

== Cultural Properties ==
=== Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property (National Designation) ===
* Itoigawa and Nō Bugaku — encompasses the {{jalink|天津神社舞楽|Q11442800}} of Itoigawa and the {{jalink|白山神社舞楽|Q11579603}} of Nō. Designated January 28, 1980 (Shōwa 55).<ref>{{国指定文化財等データベース|302|53|糸魚川・能生の舞楽}}<br/>{{国指定文化財等データベース|312|312|天津神社舞楽}}</ref>

=== Niigata Prefecture-Designated Cultural Properties ===
* Tangible cultural properties
** Wooden statue of Nunagawa-hime goddess (sculpture) — made in the late Heian period. Designated February 10, 1954 (Shōwa 29).<ref name="新潟県指定文化財">{{PDFlink|[https://www.pref.niigata.lg.jp/uploaded/attachment/130374.pdf 新潟県の文化財一覧]}}（新潟県ホームページ）。</ref>
** 3 bugaku masks (with 2 additional bugaku masks and 3 chigo-mai masks) (sculpture) — made from the late Kamakura to the late Muromachi period. Designated March 27, 1981 (Shōwa 56).<ref name="新潟県指定文化財"/>
** 3 wooden seated goddess statues (sculpture) — made from the Heian to the Kamakura period. Designated March 27, 1981 (Shōwa 56).<ref name="新潟県指定文化財"/>

=== Itoigawa City-Designated Cultural Properties ===
* Tangible cultural properties
** Amatsu Shrine main hall (structure) — designated March 26, 1991 (Heisei 3).<ref name="一覧">{{PDFlink|[指定・登録文化財一覧表]}}（糸魚川市ホームページ）。</ref>
** 2 wooden zuijin (guardian deity) statues of Amatsu Shrine (sculpture) — designated March 25, 1972 (Shōwa 47).<ref name="一覧"/>
** 2 wooden zuijin statues of Nunagawa Shrine (sculpture) — designated March 25, 1972 (Shōwa 47).<ref name="一覧"/>
** Stone seated tathagata statue (sculpture) — designated April 22, 1980 (Shōwa 55).<ref name="一覧"/>
** 2 ōkakebutsu (large hanging ornamental plaques) of Amatsu Shrine (craft work) — designated March 26, 1973 (Shōwa 48).<ref name="一覧"/>
